68	// edge-character rules are left to the server — this check only has to tell a
69	// native ref apart from things that are not one.
70	var (
71		nativeProjectRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$`)
72		nativeRepoRe    = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$`)
73	)
74	
75	// parseNativeCloneRef turns a native clone ref — `/et/<project>/<repo>` or the
76	// `<project>/<repo>` shorthand, leading slash optional — into its project and
77	// repo names. Not a match (ok == false) is not an error: the caller falls
78	// through to the mirror grammar. The `gh`/`et` forge tokens are never valid
79	// project names (3–32 chars server-side), so a two-segment ref starting with
80	// one is a malformed forge ref, not a shorthand, and is rejected here so the
81	// mirror parser can name the expected shape. Segments must match the server's
82	// name charsets: without that, any "x/y" — `git@github.com:foo/bar` included —
83	// parsed as a shorthand and produced a control-plane lookup error instead of a
84	// hint about the accepted shapes.
85	func parseNativeCloneRef(ref string) (project, repo string, ok bool) {
86		segs := strings.Split(strings.TrimPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(ref), "/"), "/")
87		if len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] == nativeCloneForge {
88			segs = segs[1:]
89		}
90		if len(segs) != 2 || !nativeProjectRe.MatchString(segs[0]) || !nativeRepoRe.MatchString(segs[1]) {
91			return "", "", false
92		}
93		if segs[0] == nativeCloneForge || segs[0] == "gh" {
94			return "", "", false
95		}
96		return segs[0], segs[1], true
97	}

99	// resolveNativeCloneURL resolves an Entire-native repo (by project and repo
100	// name) to its entire:// clone URL: name → ULID via the project-scoped lookup,
101	// then GetRepo — the one call that returns both clusterHost and path. The URL
102	// is the server's own coordinates via repoRemoteURL, never synthesized from
103	// the user's ref (note: no .git suffix — the server strips it for /gh/ paths
104	// only, so a /et/ path with it would 404).
105	func resolveNativeCloneURL(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, project, repoName string) (string, error) {
106		repoID, err := resolveRepoRef(ctx, c, repoName, project)
107		if err != nil {
108			return "", err
109		}
110		repo, err := c.GetRepo(ctx, coreapi.GetRepoParams{RepoId: repoID})
111		if err != nil {
112			return "", fmt.Errorf("get repo: %w", err)
113		}
114		cloneURL := repoRemoteURL(*repo)
115		if cloneURL == "" {
116			return "", fmt.Errorf("repo %s/%s has no clone URL yet (still provisioning?)", project, repoName)
117		}
118		// The host is server-provided but interpolated into the entire:// clone URL,
119		// so apply the same anti-token-leak guard as the mirror path (see the
120		// validateClusterHost call on the /gh/ branch).
121		if err := validateClusterHost(repo.ClusterHost.Or("")); err != nil {
122			return "", fmt.Errorf("repo has an invalid cluster host %q: %w", repo.ClusterHost.Or(""), err)
123		}
124		return cloneURL, nil
125	}
126	
127	// mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe matches the `gh/` forge token (leading slash optional)
128	// that says the user meant a mirror ref, so a malformed one gets an error about
129	// its owner/repo rather than a list of every shape `repo clone` accepts.
130	var mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^/?gh/`)
131	
132	// cloneRefShapes lists every ref shape `repo clone` accepts, for error text.
133	const cloneRefShapes = "/et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL"
134	
135	// invalidCloneRefError explains why ref matched none of the clone grammars.
136	// A GitHub URL gets pointed at the `/gh/` form it should have been; a `gh/`
137	// ref that the mirror parser rejected keeps the parser's reason (bad owner or
138	// repo charset, dot-only repo, missing segment), and anything else gets the
139	// list of accepted shapes.
140	func invalidCloneRefError(ref string, mirrorErr error) error {
141		// Hosted forms only: bare `x/y` is what the native shorthand already
142		// rejected, and a truncated `gh/foo` would otherwise read as owner "gh".
143		// The parser's dot-only guard also keeps `foo/..` out of the hint.
144		if owner, repo, err := parseHostedGitHubURL(ref); err == nil {
145			return fmt.Errorf("invalid <repo> %q: pass GitHub mirrors as /gh/%s/%s", ref, owner, repo)
146		}
147		if mirrorCloneRefPrefixRe.MatchString(ref) {
148			return fmt.Errorf("invalid <repo> %q: %w", ref, mirrorErr)
149		}
150		return fmt.Errorf("invalid <repo> %q: expected %s", ref, cloneRefShapes)
151	}
152	
153	// parseMirrorCloneRef turns a clone ref like `/gh/entirehq/entire-api` into the
154	// API provider ("github") and the lowercased owner/repo. The `gh` token is the
155	// path provider used in entire:// clone URLs; it maps to the "github" upstream
156	// provider the control plane records.
157	func parseMirrorCloneRef(ref string) (provider, owner, repo string, err error) {
158		m := mirrorCloneRefRe.FindStringSubmatch(strings.TrimSpace(ref))
159		if m == nil {
160			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("expected gh/<owner>/<repo> (leading slash optional; owner: letters, digits, '-'; repo: letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'), got %q", ref)
161		}
162		owner, repo = strings.ToLower(m[1]), strings.ToLower(m[2])
163		if gitHubDotOnlyRe.MatchString(repo) {
164			return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("repo cannot be dot-only: %s", ref)
165		}
166		return mirrorCloneProviderGitHub, owner, repo, nil
167	}

191				"  entire repo clone entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api",
192			Args: cobra.RangeArgs(1, 2),
193			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {

195				// Trim once up front so the entire:// detection and the value forwarded
196				// to git clone agree (the shorthand path trims inside parseMirrorCloneRef).

198				var targetDir string
199				if len(args) > 1 {
200					targetDir = args[1]
201				}

203				// A full entire:// clone URL already embeds the cluster host (it's what
204				// --cluster would otherwise resolve to), so pass it verbatim to git clone
205				// — no mirror lookup or cluster resolution. --cluster is irrelevant here.
206				//
207				// Deliberately NOT run through validateClusterHost: this is a raw URL the
208				// user typed, forwarded to `git clone` exactly as given (the whole point
209				// of this branch), so it's equivalent to running `git clone entire://…`
210				// directly. The validateClusterHost guard applies on the shorthand path
211				// where we *synthesize* the URL from a --cluster flag or an API-supplied
212				// host — values that flow into the STS audience under our own construction.
213				if isEntireCloneURL(ref) {
214					return runGitClone(cmd.Context(), cmd, ref, targetDir)
215				}
216	
217				// Native ref: resolve the repo's home cluster via the active-context
218				// control plane and clone from there. A native repo lives on exactly
219				// one home cluster, so --cluster has nothing to choose between.
220				if project, repoName, ok := parseNativeCloneRef(ref); ok {
221					if cluster != "" {
222						return fmt.Errorf("--cluster applies to /gh/ mirror refs; %s/%s is cloned from its home cluster", project, repoName)
223					}
224					var cloneURL string
225					if err := runCore(cmd, func(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client) error {
226						url, err := resolveNativeCloneURL(ctx, c, project, repoName)
227						if err != nil {
228							return err
229						}
230						cloneURL = url
231						return nil
232					}); err != nil {
233						return err
234					}
235					return runGitClone(cmd.Context(), cmd, cloneURL, targetDir)
236				}

238				// provider is always "github" for the /gh/ shorthand; the pull-gated
239				// resolver pins the provider itself, so it's not threaded through.
240				_, owner, repo, err := parseMirrorCloneRef(ref)
241				if err != nil {

245				var placements []coreapi.ResolvedPlacement
246				lister := func(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client) error {
247					ps, err := resolvePullablePlacements(ctx, c, owner, repo)
248					if err != nil {
249						return err
250					}
251					placements = ps
252					return nil
253				}

255				// than the active context, whose mirrors the active-context core can't

257				// different context is active failed with "not mirrored on ..."). Dial
258				// the core fronting that cluster — discovered from its well-known and
259				// authenticated with the matching local context, the same path
260				// `mirror create <url> [cluster]` uses — so the lookup resolves against
261				// the right federation. With no --cluster, list from the active context.
262				runWithCore := runCore
263				if cluster != "" {
264					if err := validateClusterHost(cluster); err != nil {
265						return fmt.Errorf("invalid --cluster: %w", err)
266					}
267					runWithCore = func(cmd *cobra.Command, fn func(context.Context, *coreapi.Client) error) error {
268						return runCoreForCluster(cmd, cluster, fn)
269					}
270				}
271				if err := runWithCore(cmd, lister); err != nil {
272					return err
273				}

275				if len(placements) == 0 {
276					return fmt.Errorf("no mirror found for /gh/%s/%s; run 'entire repo mirror create github.com/%s/%s' to onboard it", owner, repo, owner, repo)

279				chosen, err := selectCloneTarget(cmd, placements, cluster)

282				}

284				// chosen.ClusterHost is server-provided, but it's interpolated into the
285				// entire:// clone URL just like the user-supplied --cluster, so apply the
286				// same anti-token-leak guard (validateClusterHost) before building it —
287				// defense-in-depth against a malformed host reaching git / the STS audience.

293			},
294		}
295		cmd.Flags().StringVar(&cluster, "cluster", "", "Cluster host to clone from when the repo is mirrored on more than one (may belong to another auth context)")
296		return cmd

299	// mirrorLister is the subset of the control-plane client listMirrorsForRepo
300	// needs. Narrowing to an interface lets callers (e.g. resolveCurrentRepoID in
301	// api_cmd.go, and entireapi_client.go's currentRepoRef) inject a fake control
302	// plane in tests; *coreapi.Client satisfies it.
303	type mirrorLister interface {
304		ListMirrors(ctx context.Context, params coreapi.ListMirrorsParams) (*coreapi.ListMirrorsOutputBody, error)
305	}
306	
307	// listMirrorsForRepo returns every mirror placement of one upstream repo across
308	// clusters. The list API filters by provider+owner server-side but has no repo
309	// filter, so the repo match is applied client-side (owner is already lowercased
310	// to match what the server persists).
311	func listMirrorsForRepo(ctx context.Context, c mirrorLister, provider, owner, repo string) ([]coreapi.Mirror, error) {
312		all, err := fetchAllPages(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, cursor string) ([]coreapi.Mirror, string, error) {
313			params := coreapi.ListMirrorsParams{
314				Provider: coreapi.NewOptString(provider),
315				Owner:    coreapi.NewOptString(owner),
316			}
317			if cursor != "" {
318				params.PageToken = coreapi.NewOptString(cursor)
319			}
320			out, err := c.ListMirrors(ctx, params)
321			if err != nil {
322				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("list mirrors: %w", err)
323			}
324			return out.Mirrors, out.NextPageToken.Or(""), nil
325		})
326		if err != nil {
327			return nil, err
328		}
329		matched := make([]coreapi.Mirror, 0, len(all))
330		for _, m := range all {
331			if strings.EqualFold(m.Repo, repo) {
332				matched = append(matched, m)
333			}
334		}
335		return matched, nil
336	}

338	// resolvePullablePlacements returns every cluster placement of one GitHub
339	// upstream the caller may pull (clone). It backs `repo clone /gh/<owner>/<repo>`
340	// and deliberately differs from listMirrorsForRepo: that reads the
341	// affiliation-scoped mirror list (repo#list), which omits public mirrors the
342	// caller holds no grant on, so the shorthand used to fail on a public repo that
343	// clones fine by full entire:// URL. This hits the pull-gated /mirrors/placements
344	// endpoint instead — the same authority the clone's STS exchange enforces — so
345	// anything clonable resolves, public or private-with-grant.
346	//
347	// owner/repo arrive already lowercased from parseMirrorCloneRef; the server
348	// matches case-insensitively regardless. An empty result means not mirrored or
349	// not pullable, and the caller surfaces that.
350	func resolvePullablePlacements(ctx context.Context, c *coreapi.Client, owner, repo string) ([]coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, error) {
351		out, err := c.ResolveMirrorPlacements(ctx, coreapi.ResolveMirrorPlacementsParams{
352			Provider: coreapi.ResolveMirrorPlacementsProviderGithub,
353			Owner:    owner,
354			Repo:     repo,
355		})
356		if err != nil {
357			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve mirror placements: %w", err)
358		}
359		return out.Placements, nil
360	}

362	// placementPicker adapts selectPlacement's messages to the calling verb. The
363	// picker logic is identical for every consumer (dedupe by host, honor an
364	// explicit selector, prompt only when there's a real choice); only the words
365	// differ, so they're passed in rather than duplicated per command.
366	type placementPicker struct {
367		// selector names the non-interactive way to choose a cluster, as the user
368		// would type it (e.g. `--cluster`). Interpolated into the no-terminal error
369		// so the pointer names a flag the calling command actually accepts.
370		selector string
371		// title is the interactive single-select's prompt.
372		title string
373		// action names the operation in the cancellation message, capitalized
374		// ("Clone", "Remote update") — handleFormCancellation prints
375		// "<action> cancelled."
376		action string
377	}

379	// selectCloneTarget resolves which mirror placement to clone from, with the
380	// clone verb's wording. See selectPlacement for the selection rules.
381	func selectCloneTarget(cmd *cobra.Command, placements []coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, clusterFlag string) (coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, error) {
382		return selectPlacement(cmd, placements, clusterFlag, placementPicker{
383			selector: "--cluster",
384			title:    "This repo is mirrored on more than one cluster — pick one to clone from",
385			action:   "Clone",
386		})
387	}

389	// selectPlacement resolves which mirror placement a verb should act on. With one
390	// placement it returns it directly. With an explicit clusterSel it picks the
391	// matching one (or errors listing the available hosts). With more than one and no
392	// selector it prompts interactively, failing fast with a p.selector pointer when
393	// there's no terminal.
394	func selectPlacement(cmd *cobra.Command, placements []coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, clusterSel string, p placementPicker) (coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, error) {
395		// Dedupe by cluster host: one placement per cluster is what a caller acts on,
396		// and the same host appearing twice would only confuse the picker. Key on the
397		// case-folded host — DNS is case-insensitive, so a selector value differing
398		// only in case from the API's ClusterHost must still match (the alternative is
399		// a misleading "not mirrored on ..." after a successful lookup + dial).
400		byHost := make(map[string]coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, len(placements))
401		hosts := make([]string, 0, len(placements))
402		for _, p := range placements {
403			key := strings.ToLower(p.ClusterHost)
404			if _, seen := byHost[key]; seen {
405				continue
406			}
407			byHost[key] = p
408			hosts = append(hosts, key)
409		}
410		sort.Strings(hosts)
411	
412		if clusterSel != "" {
413			match, ok := byHost[strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(clusterSel))]
414			if !ok {
415				return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("repo is not mirrored on %q; available: %s", clusterSel, strings.Join(hosts, ", "))
416			}
417			return match, nil
418		}
419	
420		if len(hosts) == 1 {
421			return byHost[hosts[0]], nil
422		}
423	
424		if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
425			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("repo is mirrored on %d clusters; pass %s to choose one of: %s", len(hosts), p.selector, strings.Join(hosts, ", "))
426		}
427	
428		options := make([]huh.Option[string], len(hosts))
429		for i, h := range hosts {
430			options[i] = huh.NewOption(mirrorCellLabel(byHost[h]), h)
431		}
432		var selected string
433		form := NewAccessibleForm(
434			huh.NewGroup(
435				huh.NewSelect[string]().
436					Title(p.title).
437					Options(options...).
438					Value(&selected),
439			),
440		)
441		if err := form.RunWithContext(cmd.Context()); err != nil {
442			// handleFormCancellation prints "<action> cancelled." and returns nil for a
443			// Ctrl+C / cancelled-context abort. Surface that as a SilentError so the
444			// caller stops instead of falling through to act on a zero-value target
445			// (the `entire:///gh/...` empty-host bug) without main.go reprinting the
446			// message handleFormCancellation already wrote; a real form error propagates.
447			if cerr := handleFormCancellation(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), p.action, err); cerr != nil {
448				return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, cerr
449			}
450			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, NewSilentError(fmt.Errorf("%s cancelled", strings.ToLower(p.action)))
451		}
452		match, ok := byHost[selected]
453		if !ok {
454			// The form succeeded but handed back a host that is not on offer. Nothing
455			// has been printed here, so this must NOT be a SilentError — main.go
456			// suppresses those, and the command would exit non-zero with no message.
457			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("no cluster selected from the %d offered", len(hosts))
458		}
459		return match, nil
460	}

462	// mirrorCellLabel is the human label for a mirror placement in the clone picker:
463	// the physical cell and jurisdiction when known, always anchored by the cluster
464	// host that goes into the clone URL.
465	func mirrorCellLabel(p coreapi.ResolvedPlacement) string {
466		cell := strings.TrimSpace(p.Cell.Or(""))
467		jur := strings.TrimSpace(p.Jurisdiction.Or(""))
468		switch {
469		case cell != "" && jur != "":
470			return fmt.Sprintf("%s (%s) — %s", cell, jur, p.ClusterHost)
471		case cell != "":
472			return fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s", cell, p.ClusterHost)
473		default:
474			return p.ClusterHost
475		}
476	}

478	// runGitClone shells out to `git clone <cloneURL> [target-dir]`, wiring the
479	// child's stdio through so git-remote-entire's auth prompts and clone progress
480	// reach the user. A clone failure is wrapped as a SilentError: git already
481	// printed its own diagnostics, so main.go shouldn't reprint the wrapper.
482	func runGitClone(ctx context.Context, cmd *cobra.Command, cloneURL, targetDir string) error {
483		args := []string{"clone", cloneURL}
484		if targetDir != "" {
485			args = append(args, targetDir)
486		}
487		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), "Cloning %s\n", cloneURL)
488		gitCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
489		gitCmd.Stdin = cmd.InOrStdin()
490		gitCmd.Stdout = cmd.OutOrStdout()
491		gitCmd.Stderr = cmd.ErrOrStderr()
492		if err := gitCmd.Run(); err != nil {
493			return NewSilentError(fmt.Errorf("git clone failed: %w", err))
494		}
495		return nil
496	}

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## 1. An `/et/`-prefixed ref lost its reason

#2223 gave `invalidCloneRefError` a `^/?gh/` branch so a malformed mirror ref keeps the mirror parser's reason. There was no symmetric `^/?et/` branch, so a native ref that failed the charset check fell through to the generic shape list:

```
$ entire repo clone /et/foo_bar/dogbark
invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": expected /et/<project>/<repo>, <project>/<repo>, /gh/<owner>/<repo>, or a full entire:// URL
```

The user typed exactly `/et/<project>/<repo>` and was told to type `/et/<project>/<repo>` — the same self-contradiction #2223 set out to remove, reproduced on the other side. `parseNativeCloneRef` now returns an error rather than a bool, `invalidCloneRefError` grows the `et/` branch, and the message names the rule that was broken:

```
invalid <repo> "/et/foo_bar/dogbark": project "foo_bar" must be 3-32 characters of letters, digits and '-', not starting or ending with '-'
invalid <repo> "/et/paul/dog_bark":   repo "dog_bark" must be 1-64 characters of letters, digits, '.' and '-', not starting or ending with '.' or '-', and with no consecutive dots
invalid <repo> "/et/paul":            expected /et/<project>/<repo> or <project>/<repo> (2 names, got 1)
```

Declaring a forge token is the whole test for showing a parser's reason. A bare two-segment ref (`paul/.foo`) still gets the shape list, deliberately: it declared nothing, so it is equally a mangled URL — `git@github.com:foo/bar` is itself just a bad "project" name under the shorthand grammar, which is exactly the case #2223 fixed. That boundary is now pinned by a test.

The reasons name the offending segment rather than repeating the whole ref, so they avoid the shape the `gh/` branch produces (`invalid <repo> "/gh/entirehq/..": repo cannot be dot-only: /gh/entirehq/..`). The `gh/` messages are unchanged.

## 2. The native name check was looser than the server

The client accepted `^[A-Za-z0-9-]+$` / `^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$` and left everything else to the server, so `paul/..`, `paul/.foo`, `paul/foo.` and `paul/-x` all parsed as native refs and cost a control-plane round trip to be told the repo does not exist. Uppercase is still accepted, because both lookups fold case — the project through `foldProjectName`, and the repo on `lower(repo_registry.name)` in `getRepoGroupByProjectAndFullName`. The 3-char project minimum is real (`projectNameMinLen`), which is what makes the `<project>/<repo>` shorthand unambiguous; encoding it directly replaces the hand-written `gh`/`et` forge-token guard with the rule that guard was standing in for, so `ab/dogbark` is now a local shape error too. And the `..`/edge-dot bans are the reason `entire-trails.el` stays legal while `paul/..` does not.

Consecutive dots are checked outside the regex because RE2 has no negative lookahead. Interior hyphen runs and a hyphen adjacent to a dot (`dog--bark`, `dog-.bark`) are names the server accepts, so they are pinned as accepted — a per-segment regex, the tempting simplification here, would refuse them.

It is deliberately not stripped or refused at parse time: `foo.git` is a legal server repo name under the rules above (interior dot, no trailing dot, no `..`) — the same shape as `entire-trails.el`, and indistinguishable from it in the ref — so stripping could clone a different repo than the one named. The advice is attached at the lookup miss instead, the first point where the suffix is provably the cause. `noRepoNamedErr` becomes a typed error so the clone path can recognise the miss with `errors.As` instead of matching its text; its message is unchanged.

```
no repo named "dogbark.git" in that project (run `entire repo list <project>` to see names, or pass a ULID); a native ref keeps the .git suffix (it is stripped for /gh/ paths only) — retry as /et/paul/dogbark
```

The full-`entire://`-URL branch performs no lookup of ours, so it gets the same advice as a hedged note on stderr after `git clone` fails, and only for an `/et/` path carrying the suffix — a failed clone is just as likely to be auth or the network, and git has already printed the real diagnosis above it.

The name constraints **are** part of the contract, and my earlier note saying they "aren't in the contract" was wrong on both of its grounds. `internal/coreapi/spec/core.openapi.json` having `CreateProjectInputBody.name` as minLength 1 / maxLength 100 with no pattern only describes the wire shape; the resource layer enforces the real rules underneath it. The CLI's `looksLikeULID` accepts any 26 Crockford-base32 characters, while the server's `LooksLikeRawULID` (`core/model/id.go:28`) additionally requires the first character to be in `0`-`7`.
